title: Lazy Evaluation in Spark: Actions vs Transformations

scenes.line1: Why doesn't Spark run code right away?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why Spark doesn't process your data as soon as you call map or filter? Let's break down lazy evaluation.
Transformations like map or filter just build a plan. Actions like count or collect actually run the plan and return results.
Here's how it works: first, you chain transformations. Spark builds a logical plan. Only when you call an action does Spark actually run the job.

scenes.question: When does Spark run transformations?
scenes.wrong: Right after you call map or filter.
scenes.right: Only when you call an action, like count or collect. Transformations are lazy.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this trap in interviews. Spark only executes transformations when an action is triggered.
